summary: Variable accumulation window triggering intermittent p95/p99 inference latency spikes for dedicated tenant
description:
Issue summary:
AtlasHealth reports intermittent p95/p99 inference latency spikes and occasional request timeouts for short streaming requests. Spikes started after a traffic pattern change on 2026-03-12 and correlate with increased short-lived stream volume (many < 200 token sessions).

Impact:
- Multiple customer endpoints experienced elevated p95/p99 latency (observed p99 from ~180ms baseline to 2.1s).
- A small fraction (~0.5%) of requests returned 504/timeouts during peak bursts.
- Affects production workloads for 3 AtlasHealth services (triage, summary, and alerts).

Environment:
- Tenant: AtlasHealth (dedicated pool)
- Region: us-west-2 (prod)
- Models: redwood/roberta-chat-13b-q4 pinned by customer
- Time window: first observed 2026-03-12 09:20 - recurring spikes 09:20-10:40 PST each day since.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Replay synthetic short streaming traffic that opens many concurrent short streams (median 80 tokens).
2) Sustain QPS of ~60 for 5-10 minutes with bursty arrival pattern (many short sessions).
3) Observe p95/p99 latency climb and intermittent 504s.

Observed behavior:
- The continuous batcher accumulation window appears to grow unpredictably when many short streams arrive in rapid succession.
- Batches sometimes hold open longer than configured linger thresholds, leading to increased tail latency and KV-cache warmup interactions.

Expected behavior:
- Batcher should flush according to configured linger and max_batch latencies, preventing sustained p99 spikes for short streams.

Attachments:
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/latency/atlashealth-tail-latency
- Support logs and request ids attached in 'logs' field below.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-13 10:05 - Support triaged: customer observed pattern after a change in client-side retry/backoff. Assigned to SRE (Ethan).
2026-03-13 11:30 - SRE: reproduced with local replay harness using short-stream burst profile. Noted batch growth pattern on node rwd-batch-14.
2026-03-13 13:05 - Hypothesis: variable accumulation from interleaved stream open/close events causes linger accounting drift; affects batch flush decisions when streams terminate early.
2026-03-13 15:20 - Checked scheduler metrics: no GPU starvation, but continuous-batcher queue depth shows oscillation aligning with spikes.
2026-03-14 08:40 - Deployed temporary guard: reduce linger cap from 20ms to 8ms for AtlasHealth tenant in us-west-2; preliminary reduction in p95 observed during replay.
2026-03-14 09:10 - Still seeing isolated p99 spikes during sustained burst windows; investigating KV-cache warmup interplay and batcher flush prioritization.
Notes: related to but distinct from SUP-32714 (batch-merging); this incident emphasizes variable accumulation timing rather than cross-tenant merging.
logs: kv-cache: miss_rate=0.37 for shard=12 during spike window

comments: 2026-03-13 10:12 - Sofia Ramirez (Support): Customer reports p99 ~2s and occasional 504s after they changed client retry/backoff. Asking for p95/p99 graphs and request ids.

2026-03-13 11:45 - Ethan Cole (SRE): Reproduced locally with short-stream burst profile. Batcher linger skewing observed on nodes with high short stream churn. Collecting OS and batcher debug metrics.

2026-03-13 14:02 - Customer (AtlasHealth - Maya Patel): Confirmed we can run a controlled replay. We can also try pinning to an older model variant if that helps.
Customer asks if changing client concurrency patterns would be a valid workaround.

2026-03-14 09:00 - Ethan Cole (SRE): Rolled temporary tenant lint: linger_cap_ms=8. Early results show p95 reduced ~28% during synthetic bursts. Investigating next: batcher flush prioritization and KV cache warmup sequencing.
resolution: In progress. Temporary mitigation applied: tenant linger cap reduced to 8ms in us-west-2 which lowered sustained p95 during synthetic replays. No full rollback or permanent fix yet. Next steps listed in action_items.
action_items: Create and run deterministic microbenchmark harness targeting short-stream burst arrivals (owner: SRE) - ETA 2026-03-15
Instrument batcher to emit per-batch 'originating-stream-count' and precise linger accounting for postmortem analysis (owner: infra/serving-runtime) - ETA 2026-03-18
Evaluate changing flush prioritization to prefer oldest-opened streams when linger drift is detected (owner: infra) - design spike by 2026-03-20
Advise customer on short-term client changes: moderate client-side burstiness or enable small_batch_flush toggle to reduce tail risk (owner: Support)
